text: Machine learning is a way for computers to learn from data instead of following strict, pre-programmed rules. One of the most common types is supervised learning, where you give the computer labeled examples, called training data. For instance, you might show it pictures of cats and dogs, each already correctly labeled. The computer studies these examples and builds a mathematical model, which is like a set of patterns it discovers. Once the model is ready, it can make predictions on new, unseen data, such as guessing whether a new photo shows a cat or a dog. We then measure its accuracy by checking how often its predictions are correct. The goal is to keep improving the model by feeding it more and better training data, so its future predictions become even more reliable.
